A potential sleeper TNF DFS pick is Brian Thomas Jr., who found the end zone on Sunday after back-to-back games without a catch. If you expect the Ravens to struggle offensively with Fagnano and settle for field goals instead of touchdowns, then Baltimore kicker Jake Moody, another injury replacement, could be a part of your TNF DFS strategy. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills and is on injured reserve, shifting the line for this game from Ravens -3 (the lookahead) to Jaguars -9.5. That move also comes after backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) was ruled out for this game and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury. So, the Ravens are in a brutal spot as they look to get back over .500 (Baltimore is 4-4 this season) against the top team in the AFC South. Jacksonville is in a great spot to win the AFC South for the second season in a row, as no other team in the division has more than two wins in 2026. The Jags blew out the Indianapolis Colts – 42-7 – in Week 8, and they’re one of the best defenses in the league, ranking third in EPA/Play and eighth in success rate. Liam Coen’s team is a deserved favorite in this matchup, which could be a tough one to bet on with all the Baltimore injuries. Still, the SI Betting team has curated some picks for Week 9’s Thursday Night showdown, including player props for Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Here’s a breakdown of some of our favorite bets for the action to kick off the final week of the first half of the 2026 season. Jaguars second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten has played a major role on offense this season, appearing in 55.3 percent of the team’s snaps while registering at least 12 carries in every game. Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. A former No. 1 overall pick, Lawrence is in the MVP conversation this season, but he hasn’t been asked to throw the ball a ton with this Jaguars offense humming on the ground in 2026. Lawrence is averaging under 29 pass attempts per game in 2026, and he threw the ball just 14 times in a 42-7 win over Indianapolis in Week 8. Overall, the star quarterback has just two games (Weeks 5 and 6) where he even attempted 30 passes. So, with the Jaguars heavily favored on a short week, I expect a lighter workload for Lawrence against a Ravens team that has lost three straight and is staring down a lost season with Jackson sidelined. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. While replacing Jackson's dynamic dual-threat playmaking is impossible, Minter made it clear that the organization has no intention of waving the white flag. “We are looking to adjust our winning formula,” Minter noted earlier in the week, emphasizing a pivot toward a run-heavy, defensive-minded approach. To execute that strategy, Baltimore needed a steady veteran who protects the football. Enter Jacoby Brissett. The 33-year-old owns a 1.5% career interception rate—the second-lowest mark among active quarterbacks with at least 2,500 pass attempts, trailing only Aaron Rodgers (1.4%). By pairing Brissett with star running back Derrick Henry and relying on a rugged Baltimore defense, the Ravens can remain highly competitive without forcing a young rookie into emergency action. Crucially, Brissett won't be starting completely from scratch in Charm City. He reunites with Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfolk, who worked directly with Brissett during stints in Arizona and Cleveland. home.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
home.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Breaking Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell says he has ‘full movement' of lower body after scary on-field injury An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). Now sitting at 3-5, Atlanta's season rests upon the edge of a knife. Four straight games against playoff contenders await, and if the Falcons can't manage to scrape out a couple wins, their own playoff hopes will disappear. The good news is that star pass rusher James Pearce Jr. returns from suspension this week and is expected to play. That's a welcome boost to a pass rush that has been good at generating pressure, but fairly average at sacking the quarterback. They'll need that pass rush, and everything else they can muster, to slow down a lethal Bengals offense in Madrid on Sunday morning. The Falcons are currently 3-point underdogs to the Bengals in Week 9, per FanDuel. While Atlanta is technically the home team, the international game makes this a "neutral" field situation. picks.blurb: 3 bold predictions for Bengals-Falcons in Madrid - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Wemby makes NBA history First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire 3 bold predictions for Bengals-Falcons in Madrid (Sam Greene / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 4, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals landed in Madrid this morning for their overseas game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Below are some bold predictions for the matchup involving Joe Burrow, Michael Penix Jr. and the current betting markets. Joe Burrow doesn't throw an interception Burrow is coming off a three-interception game against the Titans and is in the midst of an interception-heavy season compared with his first seven games of each season from 2020 to 2026. He threw his most interceptions in a seven-game stretch in 2021, when he threw eight. Funnily enough, he was also throwing a lot of touchdowns, with 17, and completing passes at a high rate (68.9%). That isn't close to his completion percentage this season, as he leads the league at 73%. It seems that when Burrow is throwing interceptions, he's also completing passes and throwing touchdowns . Quite the double-edged sword. Atlanta has a minus-7 turnover differential and doesn't force takeaways often. Look for Burrow to bounce back against the Falcons' league-average defense and play a clean game. Atlanta is held under 13 points As mentioned before, Atlanta turns the ball over a lot. The Falcons are coming off a game in which Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions, and he is completing only 61.9% of his passes this season. The most shocking thing about the Falcons' offense is that Bijan Robinson has been held under 100 yards for four straight games, and he hasn't scored a rushing or receiving touchdown in that span. In fact, he hasn't scored a receiving touchdown since Week 1. Drake London, similarly, has struggled, with just one receiving touchdown this season, though he has eclipsed 100 yards twice, including a 9-catch, 194-yard performance in Week 3 against the Green Bay Packers. That was Penix's first game of the season, and it made many think the Falcons had found their stride, but they have since slowed, losing three of their last five. Bengals win by 10 This is basically an amalgamation of the other two predictions. The Falcons' offense is sputtering, and the defense isn't getting enough takeaways to beat a 5-2 Bengals team overseas. The return of pass rusher James Pearce Jr., who had 10.5 sacks in his rookie year, will boost Atlanta. But a motivated Bengals team that wants to prove it is better than last week's overtime win over the Titans will take care of business, covering the 3-point spread by plenty.

picks.blurb: Running of the *backs: Everyone knows what Bijan Robinson brings to the table, but what about Chase Brown? The Bengals have been overly reliant on the passing game all season long as Brown has struggled to break out. He has just two games with over 60 rushing yards for Cincinnati this season and now gets a matchup against a defense that just surrendered 310 to Tampa in Week 8, losing to a Bucs team that didn't complete a pass all afternoon. The running backs could take centerstage in Madrid. Under this roof: The Falcons proved that they aren't fans of Mother Nature in Week 8, seemingly forgetting how to play football in anything less than perfect conditions. Luckily for Atlanta, there is a roof at the Bernabéu. Perhaps that will help the Falcons bounce back after a deflating loss to the rival Bucs. Back in the nest: James Pearce Jr. completed his eight-game suspension for his involvement in a domestic incident with his ex-girlfriend, Chicago Sky forward, Rickea Jackson. He is now eligible to return for the Falcons, which could transform the team's defense. Pearce totaled 10.5 sacks in his rookie season, but his off-field troubles remain the headline. Falcons vs Bengals odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Bengals -3.5 Moneyline: Bengals -160; Falcons +140 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Falcons vs Bengals USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Bengals 30, Falcons 24 Set those alarms! After a one-week break, we've got more international action – this time in Madrid, where Cincinnati will try to make winning considerably less stressful than last week's overtime escape of Tennessee. Joe Burrow's offense can score with anybody. Unfortunately, the Bengals' defense can help just about anybody score, too. That gives the Falcons a fighting chance to rebound from Michael Penix Jr.'s four-interception disaster against the Buccaneers . Atlanta needs to feature Bijan Robinson and stop asking its quarterback to save the day. The Falcons won't be shutout again, but I trust Burrow to deliver the decisive drive in a competitive fourth quarter, further building his MVP case. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Bengals 34, Falcons 28 Good timing on the international trip for the Falcons, who probably want to get several thousand miles away from their rain-soaked shutout loss to the Buccaneers. Cincinnati likely won't trample Atlanta in similar fashion, but Joe Burrow poses a serious threat to a defense that could get burned if it can't get home against him. Michael Penix Jr. could be in line for a bounceback performance against a struggling Bengals secondary, though it might not be enough to prevail in a possible shootout. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Falcons 31, Bengals 27 The Bengals have been playing with playing with fire recently. Eventually, it will burn them. And there's a good chance that moment comes in Week 9 when they battle the Falcons in Madrid. Atlanta will be desperate to overcome an embarrassing loss in Week 8 that included four interceptions from Michael Penix Jr. during a rainy day in Tampa. Luckily, Bijan Robinson is the great equalizer and there will be no weather woes. The Falcons bounce back and leave the Bengals with questions heading into the trade deadline. Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid for a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. The Bengals have won three in a row and sit in second place in the AFC North, a half-game behind the Steelers. The Falcons have won just three games and are two games under .500 but in the NFC South that is good enough to also be within a half-game of first. The Bengals arrive in Spain after surviving one of the wildest games last weekend, a 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans that required Cincinnati to erase multiple deficits. Tennessee jumped ahead 13-0, led 21-13 in the third quarter and was still up 29-23 during the fourth, but Joe Burrow repeatedly brought the Bengals back. He connected with Mike Gesicki for a 25-yard touchdown and later found Tee Higgins for an 18-yard score with 1:17 remaining to force overtime at 36-36. Burrow then finished the comeback himself, scrambling nine yards for the game-winning touchdown in overtime. He has been the driving force behind Cincinnati’s three-game winning streak, which also includes road victories over Miami and Baltimore. He has the Bengals’ offense averaging a stout 29.4 points per game. An inconsistent offense has plagued Atlanta all season and last Sunday was no exception. Yes, their game against Tampa was played in torrential and constant rain, but the Bucs weathered the storm and won 16-0. Atlanta was held to 224 total yards, committed four turnovers and possessed the ball for only 24:44 as Tampa Bay controlled the game on the ground. Heck, Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes…and did not complete a one. Michael Penix Jr. endured a particularly rough afternoon, throwing a career-high four interceptions, while the Falcons managed just 125 net passing yards and 99 rushing yards. Tampa Bay pounded Atlanta for 324 rushing yards, including 170 and a touchdown from Bucky Irving and another 140 from Kenny Gainwell . The recent history favors the Bengals, who lead the all-time series 10-5 and have won the last three meetings. He traveled with the team to Madrid on Tuesday, and Bengals.com published a travel photo identifying him among the players on board ahead of the league's international weekend against the Atlanta Falcons . That leaves no verified reason to describe Chase as injured. The report instead points toward normal availability, though the inactive list will not be final until game day. The Week 8 outing was his strongest of the season. Chase caught 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards against the Titans, with a 30-yard long and one trip to the end zone. His 16 targets were a season high. The performance pushed his 2026 totals to 43 catches for 492 yards, and he has six touchdowns through seven games, according to NFL statistics. Joe Burrow played one of his strongest games of the season as well. He completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards against Tennessee. He threw five passing touchdowns in that game and added a rushing score. That connection gives Cincinnati every reason to involve Chase early against Atlanta. away.headline: Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation
away.blurb: Kyle Dugger (quad) continues to not practice as he heads toward another missed game this week. Fellow safety Jordan Battle was also limited again with a shoulder injury, but he's been playing through that issue in outings over the last few weeks. On the Titans' side of things, starting defensive tackle John Franklin-Meyers (groin) upgraded to limited and starting receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice for a second-straight day. Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation Skip to main content SI.COM The Bengals dropped their Thursday injury report ahead of the Titans game, and Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) got upgraded to full status on the report after not practicing due to that small issue and rest in general on Wednesday. He told the media on Thursday his ankle feels fine. Cincinnati is pretty clean besides those names. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has had to shuffle around his tight end room due to all of the injuries in recent weeks. Erick All just went on season-ending injured reserve with a torn ACL, and fellow tight end Tanner Hudson tore a pec this season as well. "Attention to detail has been really important to him," Taylor said about rookie tight end Jack Endries as he gets primed for more snaps. "Waiting for his moment, you can tell he never knew when his number was going to be called. He's really got to know three different positions and so I've got trust, just watching him operate in practice and in meetings and in training camp, that if needed, he was going to be ready to go, and there was a time where he wasn't needed because we had everybody healthy, and now's that time. So I'm not nervous at all about using him. I think he's earning the opportunity. I'm excited to watch him play." Taylor also echoed confidence in backup safety PJ Jules, who is filling in for Dugger's reserve role. "PJ brings a lot of energy. It's really important to him," Taylor noted. "He's done a great job on special teams in his roles. He stepped into safety. So when we need to continue to rely on depth at the safety position, I feel very confident in PJ and Russ (Yeast)." Cincinnati has a light practice on Friday. Published Oct 29, 2026 | Modified Oct 29, 2026 RUSSELL HELTMAN Russ Heltman is on the Bearcats and Bengals beat for On SI. away.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. home.headline: Bengals reveal who would've missed their first practice ahead of Week 9 matchup against Falcons hours after landing in Madrid
home.blurb: The Cincinnati Bengals released their first injury report ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. The Bengals arrived in Madrid, Spain early Wednesday morning and did not practice after landing, but did indicate who would've missed practice. The big name to monitor this week is cornerback DJ Turner II (heel). Turner, who left during Sunday's win against the Tennessee Titans , is officially day-to-day with his heel injury and would not have practiced Wednesday. That he made the trip to Spain at all is a promising sign for him to potentially play against Atlanta. Still, he'll likely need a full practice later in the week for Cincinnati to give him the green light. Defense end Cedric Johnson (ankle/foot) would've also been a non-participant Wednesday. Johnson also left the Titans game and did not return, but like Turner, he is in Spain with a chance to suit up Sunday morning. It would be a significant loss if either Turner or Johnson weren't able to play. Without Turner, the Bengals would likely start both DJ Ivey and Josh Newton alongside Week 1 starter Dax Hill. Neither Ivey nor Newton are trustworthy starters for an entire game, and even Hill had his fair share of struggles against Tennessee last week. Johnson is fourth in the DE rotation which just lost rookie Cashius Howell , the No. 3, to the Reserve/Injured list this week. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen would have gotten his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle would've been limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. The Falcons had a walkthrough Wednesday, making this injury report an estimation as well. DE Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Devine Deablo (forearm), and running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) all missed Atlanta's Week 8 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers due to their respective injuries. Bowman would've been a full participant, and Deablo and Robinson would've been limited. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) would've been the lone Falcon to miss practice. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The bigger issues for Indianapolis are on the offensive side of the ball where the Colts average just 20.1 points per game. Yes, it seemed obvious the Colts were waving the white flag following midweek trades of DeForest Buckner and Quentin Nelson but to make sure there was no doubt of their intentions, they endured a smack from Jacksonville on Sunday, 42-7. The Jaguars led 28-0 at halftime and finished with 366 total yards, while the Colts’ offensive woes were on full display turning the ball over three times and amassing a mere 243 yards. Daniel Jones endured a particularly rough afternoon, finishing 19-of-28 for 144 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, including a 92-yard pick-six, before Anthony Richardson replaced him late. Reports Monday indicated that Jones is expected to remain the starter against Dallas, with Richardson staying in the backup role. Sunday’s game is beyond a must-win for Dallas if they are to continue to entertain any hopes of even competing for a playoff spot. The Colts’ offense has been pedestrian on its better days, but the Cowboys have made even bad offenses look elite. And against the Colts, a banged-up secondary could be very costly as the Cowboys are running out of time to get a win streak going. home.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. home.blurb: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley (27) smiles Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026, during day four of Indianapolis Colts training camp at Grand Park in Westfield. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect OUT: Most notable for the Colts, both Sauce Gardner and Tyler Warren are off the injury report and will play in Jacksonville. Both had missed last Sunday’s loss to the Vikings; Warren missed the prior loss to Tennessee as well. Both provide much-needed boosts to a passing attack and secondary that are currently fairly thin, especially with Anthony Gould and Justin Walley both set to sit out. Gould, Indy’s primary punt returner, likely gives away to special teams ace Ashton Dulin in the return game. Walley’s absence is significant given the Colts’ backup nickel Cam Taylor-Britt is on injured reserve. It will likely be up to rookie Kapena Gushiken to hold down the slot, though defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo may switch up personnel to account for the lack of options there. The Jaguars list Jalen Huskey, a rookie who’s yet to appear in a game this season, as the backup strong safety, though third-string Kaevon Merriweather has much more NFL experience and is more likely to receive the start. Still, when Merriweather eventually rotates out, Indy’s pass game must test Huskey in his first professional action. Jakobi Meyers is listed as questionable with hamstring and ankle issues. He logged back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday but missed practice Friday, making his status for the weekend unclear. Only the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans won’t play in Week 9, giving bettors and fantasy players plenty of options to choose from in Survivor – if you’ve made it this far. In Week 8, the Dallas Cowboys were the one team that really hurt Survivor players, as they lost as a touchdown favorite at home against a frisky Arizona Cardinals team. NFL Week 8 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Dallas Cowboys (L) On the bright side for the team, the Cincinnati Bengals held on in overtime to beat the Tennessee Titans, avoiding an 0-2 week when it comes to these picks. MacMillan is getting the chance to buy back in so we can offer some differing opinions in Week 9 and upsets across the NFL in the last few weeks have decimated many Survivor Pools. In Week 9, our team is looking to two teams that are favored by six or more points, including Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs after a tough loss at the hands of the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 9 Survivor Pool Picks Kansas City Chiefs The Kansas City Chiefs have some issues finishing drives when they take on the elite teams in the NFL, but based on their running game and defense alone, they're well-suited to crush inferior teams. They'll host the New York Jets in Week 9, who can't beat the likes of the Miami Dolphins or Las Vegas Raiders. The Jets' defense has been especially bad this season, ranking 24th in opponent success rate. It's also worth noting that Kansas City doesn't have many more games this season that will make sense for Survivor. A home game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11 is the other option, but at this point, I believe in the Jets a lot less than Arizona. The Chiefs may not be as explosive as they once were, but on their home field they'll cruise past the Jets and help us advance our survivor entries to Week 10. – Iain MacMillan Dallas Cowboys I know the Dallas Cowboys and their terrible defense absolutely crushed Survivor Players (including our own Iain MacMillan) in Week 8, but I’m willing to go back to them on the road in a must-win game against the Indianapolis Colts. Indy was blown out by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8 – 42-7 – and it’s a candidate to move on from more pieces ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts haven’t been a competitive team for most of this season, starting with a 2-6 record while ranking 29th in EPA/Play on offense and 23rd in EPA/Play on defense. The Dallas defense can’t stop anyone, ranking 32nd in EPA/Play and 30th in yards per play allowed, but this offense is still elite. The Cowboys put up 30 points once again in Week 8 against Arizona, and they’re a top-10 team in EPA/Play and success rate on that side of the ball. Dak Prescott should be able to move the ball pretty easily against a Colts defense that couldn’t slow down Trevor Lawrence (three passing scores) and the Jaguars in Week 8. Indy is an easy team to fade the rest of the season with Daniel Jones clearly in over his head at quarterback. Jones has five touchdown passes, nine picks and has only completed 60.4 percent of his passes. If Dallas can’t win this game, the NFC East crown may truly be out of reach. I’ll take the Cowboys – who are six-point road favorites – to bounce back on Sunday. – Peter Dewey Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Chiefs team that is looking to halt a skid of its own. The Jets have lost three straight. They are 2-6 overall (1-3 on the road) and approaching the cellar in the AFC East. The Chiefs are 3-0 at home and 5-2 overall but have lost two in a row and sit in second in the AFC West a ½ game behind the Broncos. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. That game offers a useful blueprint for Sunday’s upset-minded Jets: withstand Kansas City’s early punch, keep Mahomes from creating explosives and turn offensive production into touchdowns rather than field goals. For the Chiefs, the larger storyline is whether they can rediscover their finishing touch after consecutive losses on the road. picks.headline: Chiefs-Jets betting line & game prediction: KC looks to get back on track
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs enter Sunday as 9.5-point favorites against the Jets at Arrowhead. Kansas City seeks to revive its ground game behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson. The prediction picks the Chiefs to beat the Jets 24-13 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs and New York Jets both need a win. Last week, the Chiefs suffered their second straight loss as the Denver Broncos rallied from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to win 28-24. The Jets suffered their third consecutive loss Sunday, falling 38-33 to the Las Vegas Raiders. How to watch Chargers at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Time Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -9.5. Behind the NYJ-KC matchup Although their goals and expectations entering the season were different, Sunday’s Chiefs-Jets game represents a fork in the road for both teams. The Chiefs entered 2026 hoping to rebound from a 6-11 season and return to the Super Bowl conversation, but their loss to Denver has turned simply winning the division into a dogfight. At the same time, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show tangible progress in his second season — or his tenure in New York could be short-lived. A home matchup against the two-win Jets presents the Chiefs with the classic get-right opportunity. Their best path to doing so lies in reestablishing the ground game. New York is 21st in the league against the run in opponent yards per game (123.6), allowing 4.0 yards per carry. During his first five games, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker averaged 133 rushing yards per game. Walker rushed for just 105 yards combined in the losses to Seattle and Denver, but he still ranks third in the NFL with 770 rushing yards. Kansas City will also look for ways to involve rookie Emmett Johnson more after his breakout performance of 143 scrimmage yards against the Broncos. “He’s a super-talented player, and he just brings joy,” quarterback Patrick Mahomes said of Johnson. “He has the right mindset, the right energy, and he wants to be great. Obviously, we have Kenneth, and he’s such a special football player — but to have someone that can come in whenever Kenneth’s tired or needs a break at all, and he can bring energy and juice, too, I think that’s a special combination those guys have there.” Mahomes suggested the Chiefs need to find additional touches for Johnson, potentially through an expanded role in the passing game. Johnson’s 73-yard receiving touchdown highlighted Mahomes’ 321-yard, three-touchdown performance in the loss. Kansas City’s passing game also saw a breath of fresh air with wide receiver Rashee Rice’s return to the lineup. Rice caught a team-high seven passes on eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown against Denver. He also appeared to have the game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter before the play was nullified by a false-start penalty . Reestablishing the ground game with Walker and Johnson could create opportunities for Rice, tight end Travis Kelce and wide receiver Xavier Worthy against a veteran Jets secondary that has recorded just one interception this season. Still, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid respects Glenn’s defensive scheme and personnel. “They’ve got some good veteran guys — whether it’s the safeties, the linebackers,” Reid said. “So you’re not going to have things that are botched up. Sometimes, you get coverages that are kind of messed up a little bit and there are holes there. They do a good job of making sure they can adjust to most things and do it accurately. And they’ve got some guys on the front that are good football players, big guys.” A Jets player to watch is rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who missed his team’s Week 8 game because of a groin injury. Bailey leads the Jets with 5.5 sacks, more than a quarter of the team’s 20 sacks this season. Reid said there’s a “good chance” left guard Kingsley Suamataia returns to the starting lineup after being benched for the second time in four games because of a “coach’s decision.” The Chiefs’ short-yardage and goal-to-go woes have been under criticism this week after a loss in Denver could have been different by dialing up a quarterback sneak. Perhaps this is the week Reid adds it back into the playbook at long last. Despite New York’s disappointing season, quarterback Geno Smith has put together his own resurgence, entering Sunday with 1,913 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions. Smith has posted a passer rating above 100 in five of his last six road games, and the Jets have gained 377 and 439 yards of offense in their past two games. Against a quarterback playing so efficiently, the Chiefs will need to generate more pressure than they did against the Broncos. Pro Football Focus credited Kansas City with just five pressures against Denver’s Bo Nix. While wide receiver Garrett Wilson’s status remains in concussion protocol, running back Breece Hall could return after missing five games. In Hall’s absence, Braelon Allen has been a fantastic replacement, recording at least 100 scrimmage yards in the last four consecutive games. Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, acquired by New York from Indianapolis in the trade that sent Sauce Gardner to the Colts, established a career high with 142 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Raiders. Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane missed Sunday’s game after aggravating his shoulder injury but returned to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday. Delane’s return is more important given Smith has been brilliant at throwing the deep ball, with 565 yards gained on passes of 20-plus air yards. Defensive end George Karlaftis said Wednesday that coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has preached the importance of developing a “killer instinct” after his unit’s forgettable recent fourth quarter. “No matter what the call is, you just got to find a way to finish,” Karlaftis said. “So I think, especially against a divisional opponent, against a great team that Denver is, when you’re up, when you’re leading, no matter what that lead is, you got to find a way to win the game as a defense. “And I know I felt that. I know the guys in the room, players and coaches, really felt that. And I think that’s something we’re going to take with us and harp on for the rest of the season.” Reid confirmed Wednesday that Harrison Butker will remain the Chiefs’ kicker against the Jets despite his 54-yard miss against Denver. Butker had made three extra points and a 45-yard field goal before pushing his final kick wide right. The Chiefs can get back on the right path and build some confidence by handling the Jets. The problems — an inconsistent pass rush, short-yardage struggles and too many penalties — have been glaring. This is a good opponent to fix all three against. Jets-Chiefs game prediction Beyond the Chiefs’ advantages in record, quarterback and overall outlook, I think this matchup gives Kansas City an opportunity to tap back into the offensive identity that worked early in the season — establishing Walker on the ground to open up everything else. Defensively, clean up the penalties and get to the quarterback. We’ve heard plenty about pressures, but Smith has been sacked 23 times this season — tied for second-most in the NFL. If not Sunday against the Jets, then when? The Chiefs use their get-right game to do just that. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs have 2 open spots on the practice squad ahead of Week 9: How will GM Brett Veach use them?
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , former Chiefs CB Nazeeh Johnson has completed his six-game PED suspension. He has also been cleared to return to football after ankle surgery in August. A former seventh-round pick out of Marshall in the 2022 NFL Draft, Johnson is a two-time Super Bowl champion with the Chiefs, winning titles after the 2022 and 2023 seasons. That kind of system familiarity matters when a team needs someone who can step in quickly without a lengthy learning curve. That said, I’m not sure a reunion is imminent if Johnson’s reps need Rapoport to announce to the world that he’s available. The Kansas City Chiefs have room to work with on their 17-man practice squad heading into Week 9. A thin cornerback group and a few injuries could shape how those spots get filled. The Kansas City Chiefs have two open spots on their 16-man practice squad heading into Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season. Both openings come from cornerback moves, giving Chiefs GM Brett Veach flexibility as the team works through injuries at several spots on the roster. When the Chiefs placed CB L’Jarius Sneed on injured reserve , they promoted CB Melvin Smith Jr. to the 53-man roster with an active roster contract. That created the first opening. On Tuesday, the team released free agent signing Kader Kohou from the practice squad, which created the second. Those two moves leave Kansas City rather depleted at cornerback on the practice squad. D’Arco Perkins-McAllister is the only player there right now. Injuries could shape the Kansas City Chiefs’ practice squad decisions The Chiefs have shuffled the practice squad several times recently. RB Nate Carter rejoined the team, LB Aiden Fisher joined the team, and their most recent signing was former Baltimore Ravens K Justin Tucker. Chiefs 2026 Practice Squad Ahead of Week 9 The Chiefs have just 15 players on the practice squad, including one international-exempt spot. How Kansas City fills the two open spots could come down to injuries at other positions. For starters, DT Peter Woods is dealing with a stinger he suffered during Week 8’s game against the Denver Broncos. The severity of that injury might push the Chiefs to add to the interior defensive line. Marcus Harris is the only interior defensive lineman on the practice squad, and the team has just three other players at the position on the 53-man roster. Harris also has only one practice squad elevation remaining after being elevated twice already this season . If the Chiefs need help up front for more than a week, they’ll need another body. A familiar face could help reinforce the Chiefs’ secondary Kansas City could also look to a familiar face to reinforce the secondary. It might not be a popular move with fans, but it follows Veach’s modus operandi. Johnson had ankle surgery in August and served his six-game suspension while a free agent. home.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
home.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. After returning to the lineup in Week 3, he suffered another setback during Wednesday’s practice ahead of the rematch with Denver. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. Stadium against the Dolphins (1-6). The NFC North is crowded with the Lions sitting third despite having but two losses. Miami is in the cellar in the AFC East. Lets get the obvious out of the way. The difference between these teams is substantial: Detroit is averaging 29.0 points and an NFL-best 395.4 yards per game, while Miami is averaging only 16.7 points and 290.0 yards. Detroit’s latest victory was arguably its most impressive of the season, a 19-15 win over the previously unbeaten Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field last Sunday. The Lions trailed 7-6 at halftime before Jahmyr Gibbs broke loose for a 30-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Minnesota regained the lead at 15-12 with 8:44 remaining, but Jared Goff responded by directing a seven-play, 69-yard drive and finding Jameson Williams for the go-ahead seven-yard touchdown with 4:35 left. Goff finished 18-of-25 for 176 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Gibbs carried 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown and Williams caught four passes for 70 yards including the decisive score. The victory came at a cost, however, as linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury and was listed as doubtful on the early Week 9 injury information. The Dolphins are coming off a game that typified their frustrating season, blowing a 13-3 halftime lead in a 24-19 loss to the New England Patriots. Malik Willis and the Miami offense were in control early, but New England erupted for 21 unanswered second-half points, including touchdown passes of 43 and 48 yards from Drake Maye , to turn the game around. Miami finally answered when Willis connected with rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. for a 35-yard touchdown with 2:04 remaining, but the Dolphins failed on the ensuing two-point conversion and New England recovered the onside kick. Willis finished 21-of-32 for 211 yards, two touchdowns and an interception but was sacked five times, while Miami managed only 269 total yards and 74 on the ground. Although the Lions and Dolphins meet infrequently, their most recent games have been surprisingly competitive. Miami leads the all-time regular-season series 8-5, but Detroit won three straight meetings from 2010 through 2018 before Miami answered with a 31-27 victory at Ford Field in 2022. That most recent meeting was an offensive showcase: Tua Tagovailoa threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, Tyreek Hill piled up 188 receiving yards and the Dolphins rallied from a 27-17 deficit to win, despite Goff throwing for 321 yards. The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. Among those listed were Jack Campbell, Cade Mays, D.J. Reed, Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph, and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph Among Five Limited Players Detroit also listed five players as limited participants Wednesday, including several important defensive contributors. Branch's limited designation is worth monitoring after he and Wonnum were both ruled out of Sunday's game with concussions following a helmet-to-helmet collision. His progression through the league's concussion protocol will be important as Detroit prepares for Miami. Joseph also appeared on the report as limited with a knee injury, although Dan Campbell said on his Tuesday radio appearance that the safety will not play against the Dolphins . "Kerby will be in practice this week," Campbell said. "We're going to try to give him some scout team reps. He's not going to play this game." The Lions continue taking a cautious approach as the safety works his way back toward game action. St. Brown's appearance with a rib injury is another situation to watch. While he was listed as limited, Wednesday's designation alone does not indicate whether his availability for Sunday is in jeopardy. The team's own report spells it out: "The Lions conducted a walkthrough on Wednesday. Practice participation designations for that day are based on estimations." Detroit's situation should become clearer once the team holds a full practice. That makes Thursday and Friday particularly important, especially for players dealing with concussions and those hoping to return from injuries suffered against Minnesota. The Lions are preparing to face Miami with several key players dealing with injuries on both sides of the football. With four estimated nonparticipants and five limited players Wednesday, Detroit's depth could be tested once again. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton ** As of Wednesday morning, Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol, which means Shedeur Sanders is QB1. ** Sunday’s Week 9 matchup at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South, but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. Plenty of positives happening with the Browns this season, but last week’s performance is not one of them. The Steelers thumped Cleveland, 27-6, in Pittsburgh. Cleveland was held without a touchdown for the first time this year, lost two fumbles, rushed for only 34 yards and surrendered eight sacks, while the Steelers piled up 200 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Forced to throw for much of the afternoon, Deshaun Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without an interception and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? away.headline: Cleveland Browns Injury Report Heading Into Week 8
away.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Cleveland Browns have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short- and long-term. The Browns will be without Jenkins for their Week 8 game against the Steelers, and he's required to miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. For Week 8, the Browns are relatively healthy, with only two players listed as questionable: cornerback Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas . Harden suffered a hamstring injury during the Browns' Week 7 but returned to the game. He was limited in practice throughout the week and is questionable against Pittsburgh. Thomas was also limited throughout the week with an ankle injury and carries a questionable designation. Howard suffered a concussion during Cleveland's Week 7 win against Tennessee and missed all three practice sessions this week. The Browns initially listed him as questionable on Friday but announced Saturday that he had cleared concussion protocol, which is a big relief considering the strength of Pittsburgh's defensive line. away.headline: Deshaun Watson Injury Update Causes Major Shift in Browns vs. Saints Odds for NFL Week 9
away.blurb: Watson took a big hit in the first quarter of Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he was cleared to return to the game. Unfortunately, the veteran quarterback started feeling concussion symptoms on Monday night and reported them to the team on Tuesday. The Saints (2-5 this season) are coming out of their bye week and looking to stay in the mix to win the NFC South this season. New Orleans is 0-4 straight up at home, so bettors may want to consider the Browns to at least cover the spread -- even if Watson doesn't play. Watson should be viewed as highly questionable for Sunday's matchup, as he'd need to clear concussion protocol to have a chance to play. Deshaun Watson Injury Update Causes Major Shift in Browns vs. Saints Odds for NFL Week 9 Skip to main content ON SI Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol, shifting the odds for the team's matchup with the New Orleans Saints in Week 9 of the 2026 season. Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol pic.twitter.com/ViiyRHMct8 As a result, the Browns are now 3-point underdogs on the road against the Saints in Week 9. Cleveland opened as a 2.5-point underdog in Week 9, so this move is either a sign that oddsmakers think Watson will still have a shot to play Sunday, or it shows how little a gap there is between Watson and backup Shedeur Sanders. The former Colorado star briefly played in Week 8 against Pittsburgh, and Sanders started several games as a rookie during the 2025 season. The Browns are off to a 5-3 start this season, and Watson has led five fourth-quarter comebacks to keep the team in the playoff hunt in the AFC. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) sidelined for the Baltimore Ravens, Cleveland's playoff chances improved despite a loss to Pittsburgh in Week 8. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. The former Pro Bowler has not found his form from his time with the Houston Texans, but he's proven to be the best option at quarterback for Cleveland in 2026. The New Orleans Saints are getting closer to seeing the debut of their first-round pick. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice on Wednesday, according to Saints reporter Nick Underhill . New Orleans selected the Arizona State product with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but a hamstring injury during training camp landed Tyson on the injured reserve list. Despite having a 2-5 record, the Saints still have the opportunity to make the playoffs in a weak NFC South division. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

home.headline: Saints Making Tough Decision Ahead of Week 9 Matchup
home.blurb: The New Orleans Saints have a big decision ahead. The Saints are tasked with deciding if first round draft pick Jordyn Tyson will return for the 2026 season. If he does, the Saints will have to decide in what role and in what capacity. According to Nick Underhill of neworleans.football, Saints head coach Kellen Moore said a decision on whether they will activate him from injured reserve will come on Wednesday of this week. That aligns with a recent report from NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN, who stated that Tyson's return is imminent and could come as early as this week against the Cleveland Browns. ... Saints Making Tough Decision Ahead of Week 9 Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Saints Making Tough Decision Ahead of Week 9 Matchup Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Tyson famously has a history of several knee injuries prior to being drafting by New Orleans. It was perhaps his biggest question mark in the draft process despite flashing athleticism and skill at Arizona State. Returning Tyson early could risk further injury, but not playing him would mean the Saints opted not to utilize their first round pick. Now, New Orleans will have to make a call on when to bring him back. Aaron Becker of Newsweek discussed the potential of Tyson returning to the lineup. Here's some of what Becker had to write on the big decision ahead for New Orleans. "The New Orleans Saints have been itching to get injured first-round rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson on the field as he has been sidelined since August with a Grade 2 right hamstring strain. The team revealed it is planning to make a decision on him very soon, though. Luckily, the division is still well within reach as the Carolina Panthers are in first place with 3-4 records, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Atlanta Falcons are at second and third position, respectively, with 3-5 records." It's not an easy decision. If you think you can win a division title, adding a quality receiver to star wideout Chris Olave could unlock plenty of offense for the team. Then again, you have to be honest about where you sit in the division. The NFC South is wide open, but the Saints are 2-5. Do the Saints have the roster to go on a run and make the postseason? Then again, you watch how the team competed against the Pittsburgh Steelers and how it performed in wins against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants, and it doesn't feel like the team is very far from being competitive against the league's best. We'll keep an eye on what the Saints elect to do with Tyson as the season progresses.

home.headline: Deshaun Watson Injury Update Causes Major Shift in Browns vs. Saints Odds for NFL Week 9
home.blurb: Watson took a big hit in the first quarter of Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he was cleared to return to the game. Unfortunately, the veteran quarterback started feeling concussion symptoms on Monday night and reported them to the team on Tuesday. The Saints (2-5 this season) are coming out of their bye week and looking to stay in the mix to win the NFC South this season. New Orleans is 0-4 straight up at home, so bettors may want to consider the Browns to at least cover the spread -- even if Watson doesn't play. Watson should be viewed as highly questionable for Sunday's matchup, as he'd need to clear concussion protocol to have a chance to play. Deshaun Watson Injury Update Causes Major Shift in Browns vs. Saints Odds for NFL Week 9 Skip to main content ON SI Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol, shifting the odds for the team's matchup with the New Orleans Saints in Week 9 of the 2026 season. Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol pic.twitter.com/ViiyRHMct8 As a result, the Browns are now 3-point underdogs on the road against the Saints in Week 9. Cleveland opened as a 2.5-point underdog in Week 9, so this move is either a sign that oddsmakers think Watson will still have a shot to play Sunday, or it shows how little a gap there is between Watson and backup Shedeur Sanders. The former Colorado star briefly played in Week 8 against Pittsburgh, and Sanders started several games as a rookie during the 2025 season. The Browns are off to a 5-3 start this season, and Watson has led five fourth-quarter comebacks to keep the team in the playoff hunt in the AFC. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) sidelined for the Baltimore Ravens, Cleveland's playoff chances improved despite a loss to Pittsburgh in Week 8. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. The former Pro Bowler has not found his form from his time with the Houston Texans, but he's proven to be the best option at quarterback for Cleveland in 2026. When Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury, the Giants, unwilling to give up on the season, traded for J.J. McCarthy, the former first-round pick who was languishing on the Vikings ' bench as the No. 3 QB. They were buyers, and they still might be as they're rumored to be in the running for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor by the Nov. 10 deadline. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets Contrast that to when Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was presumably lost for the season due to blood clots. The Eagles turned the position over to their No. 3 QB (at the start of the season) in Tanner McKee, to mixed results. And now they're benching McKee in favor of Joe Milton, who was signed off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16. The Eagles are clearly sellers at the deadline after already trading A.J. Brown and Cam Jurgens for future draft picks. As for the Giants, who are in first place in the NFC East at 4-2-1, McCarthy has shined in his five quarters of action. He threw for 252 yards in a 27-21 overtime win over the Texans in Houston on Oct. 25. The week before, McCarthy nearly led a comeback against the Saints when he replaced Jameis Winston and threw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter. The Eagles have a bye week following this NFC East clash, and I’m sure they feel it couldn’t come soon enough. Tanner McKee will make his fourth consecutive start after leading the Eagles to 14, 21, and 10 points. The offense has been injury-riddled. DeVonta Smith sat out and Saquon Barkley hobbled to 30 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. Makhi Lemon had another strong game with six catches for 57 yards, but there wasn’t much to brag about in the 27-10 loss. The Eagles jumped out to a 10-0 first-quarter lead, then allowed a 27-0 run. McCarthy . The New York offense has scored 27 points in each of the last two games and could’ve been 2-0. The Giants should be feeling good as they sit atop the NFC East, whereas the Eagles are at the bottom. Milton and McCarthy were teammates briefly at the University of Michigan. Milton played for the Wolverines from 2018 to 2020 and was there for about two weeks when McCarthy arrived as a freshman.
