Giants Add Familiar Face at Running Back as Skattebo’s Injury Status Raises Questions Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants were back to work on Monday after their Week 8 bye, but one key offensive player worked with trainers on the sideline during the media portion of practice. Running back Cam Skattebo, who said he felt something in his hamstring after his 42-yard run against the Houston Texans in overtime two weeks ago, was spotted working to the side with trainers. It’s unclear whether Skattebo is simply trying to buy a couple more days to let his hamstring fully heal before the team begins its prep for Sunday’s road game at Philadelphia, or whether the injury could limit him in practice and, potentially, the upcoming game. Head coach John Harbaugh characterized Skattebo's status as "day to day." Either way, the Giants, who last week placed running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with a hamstring injury, are not taking any chances of going into the critical division matchup with just Devin Singletary and newcomer Gregory Desrosiers, whom they signed last week off the Chargers’ practice squad. To that end, New York has signed running back Eric Gray, its fifth-round pick in the 2023 draft, to its practice squad. Gray, who was with the team this summer, appeared in 34 games over three seasons, including just four in 2025 after landing on PUP due to a knee injury. He has 31 career rushing attempts for 79 yards and caught 16 of 18 targets for 104 yards, with no rushing or receiving touchdowns. This past summer he led the team in receptions with eight catches for 54 yards. He also led the Giants in rushing with 90 yrds on 30 carries. Gray was with the Cleveland Browns practice squad in September but was released in early October. away.blurb: Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team's Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work. Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the Giants pull out a win, but it came at a price, as he picked up a hamstring injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh spoke about Skattebo's injury in more detail. His struggles led to him being benched in the team's Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints, but he redeemed himself against the Texans when he had his best game of the season. He ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants pull out a big win on the road. Should Skattebo have to sit out, it will mean an extended opportunity for Devin Singletary and newly-signed Gregory Desrosiers. Eric Gray, who was just signed to the practice squad, and Phil Mafah are running backs who would be available for elevation. home.headline: Cam Skattebo injury: Giants’ RB a question mark heading into game vs. Eagles
home.blurb: Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team's Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work. Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the Giants pull out a win, but it came at a price, as he picked up a hamstring injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh spoke about Skattebo's injury in more detail. His struggles led to him being benched in the team's Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints, but he redeemed himself against the Texans when he had his best game of the season. He ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants pull out a big win on the road. Should Skattebo have to sit out, it will mean an extended opportunity for Devin Singletary and newly-signed Gregory Desrosiers. Eric Gray, who was just signed to the practice squad, and Phil Mafah are running backs who would be available for elevation. "We're going to just have to see where we're at. I'll probably have more information toward the end of the week. We'll see on both those guys where we're at." Skattebo has had an up-and-down season for the Giants. He scored a touchdown in the team's Week 1 win against the Dallas Cowboys, but struggled to find the end zone in the next four weeks. He also recorded four fumbles in the team's first five games. Skattebo likely will have a big role when the team plays the Philadelphia Eagles this week if he is able to go.

away.headline: NFL injury update: Rams lose Jaylen Watson for 2026 season after shoulder surgery, Myles Garrett nears return
away.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
away.blurb: India, Nov. 5 -- The Los Angeles Rams have been dealt another setback on the defensive front, with cornerback Jaylen Watson ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. Head coach Sean McVay confirmed on Wednesday that Watson will undergo surgery on his right shoulder and is set to be placed on season-ending Injured Reserve. The injury comes as a significant blow to the Rams, who will now have to manage the rest of their campaign without the cornerback. Rams Cornerback Jaylen Watson to Undergo Shoulder Surgery, Ruled Out for Remainder of 2026 NFL Season Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay revealed that Jaylen Watson wanted to continue playing despite his recurring shoulder problem, but medical advice ultimately forced the team to take a different approach. According to McVay, doctors warned that "the likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability" if Watson returned to action. Although using a protective brace was considered, it would have restricted the cornerback's movement. Explaining the decision, McVay said, "It's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us." Rams Receive Injury Boost as Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Ronnie Rivers Near Return Meanwhile, the Rams have received some encouraging news regarding Myles Garrett's recovery. The franchise has opened the 21-day practice window for the defensive star, who has been recovering from arthroscopic surgery on his left knee since September. Garrett is expected to participate in limited practice sessions initially, with McVay planning to gradually increase his workload. Speaking about his return to training, the coach said, "It's great to be able to get him back out there." He also indicated that Garrett could take around half of the team's practice repetitions as the medical staff monitors his progress. The Rams have also opened the practice window for tight end Terrance Ferguson, who has missed the last five weeks with a right ankle injury. Running back Ronnie Rivers is another player expected to return after recovering from a calf problem, with McVay confirming plans to activate him from Injured Reserve. These developments provide some encouragement for Los Angeles heading into the next phase of the season. However, replacing Watson's defensive production and experience will remain a major challenge as the Rams look to maintain their position in the NFL playoff race. Watson's latest setback occurred during the Rams' Week 8 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, November 1, when he aggravated an existing shoulder problem and was forced to leave the game early. He had originally dislocated the same shoulder during Week 3 and missed the following week's action before returning to the lineup. away.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
away.blurb: While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury. The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers. “The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.” “It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.” In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams. Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back). Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury. home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.headline: Commanders-Rams Injury Report Raises New Concern on Depleted Defensive Line
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their first Week 9 injury report as the team gears up for its matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. Jer'Zhan (Johnny) Newton practiced fully on Wednesday after being limited throughout last week. A day after the team placed both starting defensive tackles on injured reserve , Shy Tuttle was limited with a shoulder injury. Newton returned to practice last week as the team opened his 21-day practice window while he recovers from a torn pectoral muscle. He was downgraded to OUT before the Eagles game, but Commanders head coach Dan Quinn likes how his return is progressing. "The arrow is going up for sure, and I'm very optimistic for it. But it's important to stack another good week of him in practice and movements." Newton must still be activated from injured reserve before he can play against Los Angeles. Treylon Burks was another name missing from Wednesday's practice, as the receiver continues dealing with the foot injury that left him questionable against Philadelphia . He played anyway and led Washington with 81 receiving yards on three catches, including a 53-yard gain. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, the Commanders need Burks available, but missing Wednesday's practice doesn't necessarily mean he'll be unavailable against Los Angeles. Stefon Diggs also sat out Wednesday, although his absence was listed as rest rather than an injury. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: WR Pat Bryant gearing up for return
away.blurb: After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster. WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers. What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday. Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up. Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/broncos/onsi as Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: WR Pat Bryant Gearing Up for Return . That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina . Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve. Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. A Potential Boost to Denver's Passing Offense Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together. Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season. With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air. away.headline: How healthy is Bryce Young? Panthers QB talks about his status as Broncos loom
away.blurb: Panthers coach Dave Canales tempered his normal enthusiasm when asked about Young Thursday night, following a 27-19 loss to Green Bay in which the quarterback was sacked six times. Discussing whether Young’s mobility had been limited by his knee in the game, the coach said: “Maybe. I would say that he certainly doesn’t look like he’s got that quick, make-you-miss type of deal, but he was able to create some space for himself. But the rush got after us, and that’s the bottom line.” With one of the NFL’s most sack-happy defenses about to enter Bank of America Stadium, Bryce Young insists he’s just fine. The Carolina Panthers (3-4) host the Denver Broncos (6-2) Sunday, and everyone involved is well aware of what’s coming. Young has been sacked 11 times in the past two games. He’s playing on a problematic left knee and he’s not escaping defenders the way he does when he’s at his best. After rushing for 200+ yards in each of his first three seasons, he’s only got 34 so far this year. “I’m good,” Young said Tuesday when asked about his nagging knee injury. “I’m capable of doing everything for the team. It’s football. You can ask anyone across the league that’s been playing… if they’re not having something. That’s part of the game. I feel good.” Now comes Denver, which whipped the Panthers in Super Bowl 50 because Carolina couldn’t handle the Broncos’ pass rush. But when the rush comes up the middle, or when it rolls in from more than one place, he’s often sacked. away.headline: Broncos rule RJ Harvey, Talanoa Hufanga out against Chiefs, slew of key players questionable
away.blurb: Jaylen Waddle, Zach Allen, Garett Bolles and Brandon Jones are all questionable to play vs. Kansas City The Broncos will be without a pair of key contributors Sunday against Kansas City and a quartet of foundational players are listed as questionable. Running back RJ Harvey will miss the game after sustaining a knee injury in Thursday's practice, while safety Talanoa Hufanga is out for a third straight game with an ankle injury. Denver is also listing defensive tackle Zach Allen (hamstring), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), left tackle Garett Bolles (hip), and safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) as questionable. All four were limited participants in practice Friday. Harvey injury is not believed to be severe or hold him out long term, a source told The Post. He's already been ruled out for the Chiefs' game, but it's an encouraging sign for the Broncos' running back. It is not immediately clear how much time he will miss or if he is a candidate for injured reserve. Denver typically places players on IR on Saturday before a game. With Harvey out Sunday and fellow running back Tyler Badie already on injured reserve with a thumb issue, the Broncos will rely heavily on rookie Jonah Coleman and veteran J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. They are also likely to promote Cody Schrader from the practice squad and have at times used fullback Adam Prentice as a pass protector this year. Broncos WR Pat Bryant practices fully, tracking toward return from IR “I’m ready for any opportunity I’m given,” he said. “Whenever I'm out there, I’m going to give the team my all.” Hufanga, meanwhile, was present at Denver’s practice Friday for the first time since he hurt his ankle Oct. 11 at the Los Angeles Chargers. He was listed as a non-participant, however. With Hufanga out and Jones questionable, the Broncos will elevate veteran Taylor Rapp for the third and final time from the practice squad unless he is promoted to the 53-man roster before Sunday. He has filled in ably the past two weeks with Hufanga down. Waddle and Allen were injured in the fourth quarter of last week’s win at Arizona while Jones dropped out of Thursday’s practice with the hamstring issue. The fact that they and Bolles both practiced in a limited capacity over the past two days is a promising sign, though there is enough uncertainty about their game statuses to list them as questionable. Jones practicing one day after dropping out with a hamstring issue is also a positive sign. Kansas City's list of players up in the air for Sunday isn't as long as Denver's, but several key defenders are either out or questionable. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed was ruled out by the team Friday with a knee injury while a pair of standout rookies in cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and edge rusher R Mason Thomas (personal) are questionable to play. That’s the good news; the bad news is that two new names popped up on the injury report. Both were limited, though, so there’s no reason to fear for their Week 8 availability quite yet. Meanwhile, it’s great to see Allen and Waddle progress to limited on Thursday after being held out of Wednesday’s session. Both starters went down late in last week’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. If the Broncos are going to avenge their ugly 31-10 loss in the season opener, they’ll need a little luck on the health front. Let’s take a look at Thursday’s practice report. Patrick Surtain II | CB (Ankle) If Harvey is compromised this week, at least the Broncos have Jonah Coleman back. Coleman can pound the rock and doesn’t have to leave the field on third down because of his receiving and pass-protecting proficiency. Plus, J.K. Dobbins is more than capable of doing it all, too. Let’s hope it doesn’t come to that. With Hufanga still not participating in practice, it’s not looking great for him this week. Friday will be the ultimate decider, but that’s why the Broncos really need Jones to take it easy on his hamstring. The thought of going against Patrick Mahomes without either of your starting safeties is enough to make any team sweat a bit. Devon Key is healthy, and Taylor Rapp has done well in playing starter snaps since Hufanga got hurt, but the Broncos would much rather have their starters against Kansas City, or at least one of them. Jones is midway through what has easily been his best as a Bronco since joining the team in 2024. If the Broncos beat the Chiefs at Mile High, they’ll take the lead in the AFC West. Dener’s road ahead is significantly easier than Kansas City’s. The Broncos have a few toughies left on the schedule beyond Week 8, but the Chiefs still have to face the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and New England Patriots. home.headline: 7 Injuries to Monitor for Panthers: Good News on the Horizon?
home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers have arguably been the most injured team all season. They've lost four cornerbacks, their top two edge rushers, both starting tackles, a starting guard, the second running back, the third wide receiver, their prized rookie wide receiver, and more. Those players are all out right now. On Tuesday, Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks both got some work in on the side. So did Mike Jackson. The Panthers reportedly plan to open the 21-day return window for Brooks and Legette sooner rather than later. Joe Person reported that Jaelan Phillips and Jaycee Horn were also working off to the side. Horn hasn't played since Week 3, and Phillips has been out the last couple of weeks. The Panthers officially opened the 21-day return window for Brady Christensen. They want him to get his feet under him first, but he could potentially be in the lineup sooner rather than later. At times, they've been without Devin Lloyd, Bobby Okereke, Jalen Coker, Monroe Freeling, Bobby Brown, and Pat Jones. It has been a bloodbath, and one could reasonably argue that it has played a hand in their 3-4 record. After a "mini-bye," so to speak, the Panthers are back in action this week ahead of an important matchup with the Denver Broncos . And fortunately, there are some positive rumblings in the injury world for once. Panthers are beginning to get some good injury news Through seven contests, the Panthers have honestly dropped like flies. Starting in Week 3, it seems like every single game costs a player a trip to the IR or at least a couple of games on the bench, unable to suit up. That didn't end last week, with Will Lee III going down. He may avoid the IR, but he probably won't play this week. It's just been that kind of season, which is a shame given the talent this roster actually has when it's healthy. Regardless, though, things may be beginning to turn in Carolina's favor. There are several injuries to monitor this week, and there is plenty of good news that seems to be on the horizon. And perhaps the best update of all: Bryce Young hasn't missed any snaps, but he has clearly been hobbled by a knee injury, sapping his mobility. Young said he's "good," although he has never said it's been a problem. Dave Canales said it was hampering his quarterback, and on Tuesday, the coach said Young was "ready to rock," and reports suggest that Young's mobility is much improved. home.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
home.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
home.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. Hubbard doesn't have top-level breakaway speed, but he's tough and normally does the little things right and finds way

He could play as early as this Sunday and was a full participant. There are several players who were held out today: Kris Abrams Draine, Talanoa Hufanga, Brandon Jones, and Eyioma Uwazurike were all non-participants. away.headline: David Montgomery Injury Clouds Texans' Offensive Outlook Following Slow 2-5 Start
away.blurb: With offensive questions to answer in the offseason, the Texans went out and got the RB1 they were needing. That guy was David Montgomery, a seven-year veteran from the Detroit Lions. He was signed to a two-year, $16.5 million contract. It remains to be seen how long Montgomery will be out for, but the signing of Pitsenberger might not be very encouraging for the former's Week 9 status. David Montgomery Injury Clouds Texans' Offensive Outlook Following Slow 2-5 Start - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Tate Mosher · Athlon Sports Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:45 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads After a mostly dominant 2025 NFL season, the Houston Texans have come crashing down in 2026. The team finds themselves at 2-5 following Week 8 of the season. That has them in second place in the AFC South and three games behind the Jacksonville Jaguars. In a reversal from last season, it is the team's defense that is holding them back. They are allowing 24.3 points per game (18th in NFL). That is a large change from 2025, when they allowed only 17.4 a game (2nd in NFL). Houston Texans running back David Montgomery (32) Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Outside of a three-touchdown performance in Week 1, Montgomery has been largely ineffective. Across five games this season, he has taken the ball 52 times for only 138 yards, resulting in a poor 2.7 yards per carry. During Week 5, the free agent acquisition pulled his groin in a game at the Tennessee Titans. He has been sidelined since. On Monday, the Texans signed RB Joshua Pitsenberger to the practice squad, per Jonathan M Alexander of the Houston Chronicle. Moments after this transaction was reported, Houston head coach Demeco Ryans said he did not have any significant update on Montgomery's health. His status for Week 9 appears to be in jeopardy. Pitsenberger is a 2026 undrafted free agent whom the Texans signed briefly after the draft. He has yet to appear in an NFL game but now becomes the fifth running back on the team, active roster and practice squad included. Houston has three RBs on the active roster, that being Woody Marks, Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale. The offense this season has largely relied on the arm of quarterback C.J. Stroud. away.blurb: Not just their versatile nickel, Jalen Pitre, but also starting strong safety Reed Blankenship as well, who's been deemed out since he went down with a concussion during the second quarter of Houston's Week 6 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. We'll know more about Blankenship's status now and moving forward once the Texans are back practicing on Wednesday, and we get an injury report designating the veteran safety as a full, limited, or non-participant. A concussion absence typically lasts around one to three weeks for most players around the league, but with Blankenship's newly discovered hand surgery, there's a chance that it takes more time for him to return as a starter on the back end of the Texans' defense. For any time that Blankenship is set to remain out for the Texans' secondary, the name to keep an eye on will be veteran MJ Stewart, who returned from his lengthy absence due to a quad injury earlier this year, and was elevated to a starter last week against the Giants as a plug-and-play replacement. However, it was also revealed from the Texans' Week 7 injury report before facing the New York Giants that Blankenship was dealing with a hand injury –– one that wasn't exactly seen when the veteran safety went down against the Jaguars, but an issue that added to his troubles to get back on the field nonetheless. And it seems like, leading up to the Texans' Week 8 game against the LA Chargers, we now know a bit more about the status of Blankenship. What We Know About Reed Blankenship's Injury According to Jonathan M. Alexander of The Houston Chronicle , Blankenship had surgery on his left hand "not long after" the Texans' win over the Jaguars in Week 6. Alexander also notes that Blankenship is still in concussion protocol heading into the week against the Chargers, and will be a name to monitor as the week progresses. Texans safety Reed Blankenship, who remains in concussion protocol, also had surgery on his left hand not long after the Jaguars game, per a source. The Texans will see how he progress through the week. Blankenship was one of the Texans' biggest offseason additions brought in several months ago one a three-year contract, and was expected to bring an added sense of stability within an already strong Houston secondary. Minnesota is No. 1 in points allowed (13.3) and No. 2 in total defense (271.6). picks.headline: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Wemby makes NBA history First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. picks.blurb: The Patriots are likely to be on A.J. Brown watch once again. After the receiver missed Sunday's win over the Dolphins with a knee injury, Mike Vrabel said Monday that the team would need to see how Brown progresses before determinig his status for the upcoming tilt. Micah Parsons is expected to make his much-anticipated return to practice this week for the Packers, but he might still be a long way out from contributing. Matt LaFleur said the edge rusher might need the full 21-day window before being added to the active roster, which would mean a late November return. If there is any change to running back Josh Jacobs' disciplinary status, it won't come from the Packers. LaFleur said this week that the team plans to continue on with the ball carrier as the NFL extends its investigation. Patriots vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Patriots -3.5 Moneyline: Patriots -160; Packers +145 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Patriots vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Patriots 24, Packers 23 The Patriots are 17-0 with Drake Maye when favored by at least a field goal and we just may close there by Sunday afternoon. Who am I to disagree with a great trend? The Packers possess a dynamic passing offense but, even with Josh Jacobs back, still can't run the football with any efficiency. Plus, Christian Watson is dealing with a rib injury that sent him to the hospital for a portion of last week's primetime win over the Panthers. The Pats have the personnel to take advantage defensively, but Maye's offense also has questions around injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and others. I'll take New England at home, but I'm expecting nervous pacing around living rooms throughout Massachusetts before this one is settled. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Packers 28, Patriots 27 Bombs away. With a matchup of two daring downfield passers and lackluster run games, both teams could air it out early and often against one another. Between their reliance on Jordan Love connecting on vertical shots and the pass rush picking up the rest of the defense with pressure, Green Bay might be more reliant of the two on igniting big plays. But the Packers' explosiveness shouldn't be doubted, and it could lead the team to its fifth win in six games. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 26, Patriots 23 Good luck figuring these teams out. At times, Green Bay looks like a bad team. Then it looks like a Super Bowl contender. The same is true of New England, meaning there is a large range of outcomes we could see in Week 9. Will A.J. Brown play for the Patriots? Does it matter? Drop issues have plagued the star receiver and there's no sign of that disappearing anytime soon. On the other side, Christian Watson made 'Thursday Night Football” look like the WWE with his dramatic return. In the end, we'll trust the Packers offense to be the difference. New England’s defense will be put to the test this week after facing the Dolphins on the road last week (24-19). New England’s defense ranks ninth in points per game allowed (20.3) and 11th in third-down defense (38.5%). The Patriots’ last three wins have come over the Dolphins, Jets, and Raiders, and they only have two wins against teams with a winning record (BUF, PIT). This game smells like one that could come down to the final possession. One area New England has struggled in is the turnover margin. New England is a -0.9 team turnover margin per game, ranking tied for second-worst with the Chargers, ahead of only the Colts (-1.4). He’s thrown the ball 40-plus times in three straight games and five out of eight on the year. The running game is starting to come around with Josh Jacobs back, but Jacobs hasn’t alleviated the pressure from Love yet. Jacobs had 36 and 39 rushing yards on 11 and 21 carries. away.blurb: Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable The Green Bay Packers added cornerback Keisean Nixon to the injury report before Thursday night's showdown with the Carolina Panthers . The team says Nixon is questionable to play with a shoulder injury. Nixon joins four other questionable players for the Packers: receiver Matthew Golden (foot/shoulder), defensive linemen Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr. (quad). Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and right guard Travis Glover (knee) have all been ruled out for Thursday night. Not having Nixon available on Thursday night would push either Carrington Valentine or Benjamin St-Juste into the starting lineup opposite rookie Brandon Cisse. St-Juste is expected to return after missing two games with a hamstring injury. Kamal Hadden is also available at corner. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. Rookie Jermod McCoy took over for him at outside corner . The team then listed Porter as questionable with a groin injury . The injury came at MetLife Stadium against the Jets in Week 8, and it leaves the Raiders watching the sideline to see whether a key cornerback can come back. Jets quarterback Geno Smith hit wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a long completion to start the game, with accounts of the gain ranging from 31 to 41 yards. Porter hit the turf without being touched , according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal . Trainers helped Porter to the medical tent on the Raiders' sideline with the score still 0-0. He later emerged and was trying to regain his mobility under trainers' watchful eyes, according to Raiders beat writer Sam Warren. Why Isn’t Fernando Mendoza Playing for the Raiders Today? Insider Gives Timeline Las Vegas Raiders' Darien Porter Career Background Porter, 25, was born Jan. 6, 2001, in Bettendorf, Iowa, and is listed at 6 feet 2 inches and 195 pounds . He played receiver and cornerback at Bettendorf High School, catching 27 passes for 440 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior, and won a Class 4A state title in the 400 meters. He spent time at Iowa State from 2019 through 2024 , starting at receiver before moving to defensive back. Special teams made up most of his early role. He became a full-time starter in 2024, finishing with 18 tackles, two tackles for loss, three interceptions and two passes defended, and earned honorable mention All-Big 12 recognition. Porter ran an unofficial 4.30-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine. The Raiders selected Porter in the third round of the 2025 draft, 68th overall. As a rookie, he played all 17 games, starting 10 , and totaled 42 tackles, three passes defended and one fumble recovery. His rookie contract runs through 2028 . This season, Porter missed Week 2 against the Chargers because of a foot injury against the Dolphins in the opener. That was a separate issue from Sunday's injury. Before it, he had been targeted five times in that opener and allowed one catch for 12 yards , according to Pro Football Focus . home.headline: San Francisco 49ers coach shuts down reunion talks as Brandon Aiyuk seeks NFL reinstatement
home.blurb: Aiyuk filed for NFL reinstatement this week alongside new agent Drew Rosenhaus and is scheduled to report Friday, though the 49ers do not plan to retain him. While general manager John Lynch previously struck a softer tone regarding a potential return for the expensive wideout, Shanahan’s position has remained firm. Beyond mocking Shanahan’s demeanor and leadership, Aiyuk drew severe backlash for taking thinly veiled jabs at Shanahan’s car accident in July , posting Instagram stories telling him to "stay in yo own lane" and declaring that "you can't win the race if you crash out." Brandon Aiyuk won't be getting a warm welcome back in San Francisco after walking away from the team and embarking on an erratic, self-destructive stretch that has effectively alienated him from the NFL. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan officially slammed the door on a reunion Wednesday. Despite San Francisco’s depleted receiver room, the organization has no intention of bringing Aiyuk back, even after the former All-Pro claimed he is cleaning up his act. When asked Wednesday about Aiyuk's apparent turnaround, Shanahan was blunt. "None. I have no expectation," Shanahan said. "I’ve kind of moved on with that mentally and doing kind of how I talked to you guys two months ago. Nothing’s really changed for me." Aiyuk spent months burning bridges across the organization. He severed ties with the franchise through an acrimonious contract standoff, an off-field reckless speeding citation and completely ghosting team medical staff during injury rehabilitation. After San Francisco voided his future contract guarantees and sidelined him, Aiyuk went scorched-earth on social media . He blasted the organization as "stupid," accused Lynch of showing up uninvited at his home and hurled insults at front-office personnel and assistant coaches. Before the fallout, Aiyuk stood as one of San Francisco’s most dynamic offensive playmakers. Selected 25th overall in the 2020 NFL Draft, he developed into the team’s primary perimeter target, posting consecutive 1,000-yard receiving campaigns in 2022 and 2023. His peak came in 2023, when he earned Second-Team All-Pro honors after amassing 1,342 receiving yards and playing a pivotal role in San Francisco’s run to Super Bowl LVIII. Across five seasons in the Bay Area, Aiyuk totaled 294 receptions for 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns. Under contract through 2028 with $27 million in guarantees already voided, releasing Aiyuk leaves San Francisco with a $12.35 million dead-cap hit, finally clearing the path for him to pursue opportunities elsewhere. home.headline: AWOL NFL star files for bombshell return to 49ers roster... despite active arrest warrant
home.blurb: Even if he is reinstated, however, Aiyuk is unlikely to ever return to the field for the 49ers. According to ESPN, the most likely outcome is San Francisco releasing him. Shanahan was asked Wednesday what his response was to news of Aiyuk's planned return. 'None,' he said. 'I have no expectation. I've kind of moved on with that mentally... nothing has really changed for me.' 'You can't win the race if you crash out,' Aiyuk said about Shanahan, who suffered a broken hand, three broken ribs and a concussion in a crash that nearly cost him his eye. MORE: NFL bad boy Dre Greenlaw handed huge fine for sucker-punching rival Exiled NFL star Brandon Aiyuk has filed paperwork to be reinstated, with the 49ers wide receiver reportedly expected back at the practice facility on Friday. That is despite Aiyuk being the subject of an active arrest warrant in Santa Clara County - where the 49ers' facility is situated - after he was allegedly caught driving at 104mph outside Levi's Stadium earlier this year. Aiyuk has not played an NFL game since tearing knee ligaments in October 2024, with many fearing for his future after a chaotic offseason saw him fail to report for training camp and threaten to tank his career to force an exit from San Francisco. He is on the 49ers' reserve/did not report list but Aiyuk's new agent said Wednesday that the wide receiver is now plotting a comeback. 'Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,' Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN . Both general manager John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan have suggested the wide receiver will not play another game for the 49ers. While the receiver is on the reserve/did not report list, the 49ers do not have to pay Aiyuk or make a spot for him on their roster. San Francisco previously voided $27 million guaranteed in Aiyuk's contract for 2026 after he failed to participate in meetings and other team activities last summer while rehabilitating his knee injury. In fact, Aiyuk has collected only $48.1 million of his four-year, $120 million contract extension. He was due a $24.9 million option bonus on September 1. The 28-year-old has faced significant criticism over his antics and posts on social media in recent months, including crude jokes he made about Shanahan's offseason car crash. Aiyuk had fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until Rosenhaus said on Monday that he had been hired. The receiver has previously suggested he wants to play alongside his former college teammate Jayden Daniels on the Washington Commanders.

So, we had to agree on some things to at least make it close enough to be able to talk to him. And when we got on a FaceTime with JJ, it went well. ... away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Breaking Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell says he has ‘full movement' of lower body after scary on-field injury An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). away.blurb: Macdonald clarified it is the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said. The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Bleacher Report • 17h Malachi Toney Out 4 Weeks Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, head coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday. Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week. Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1). A win this week over the Cardinals (3-5) would increase the defending champions' playoff odds to 54 percent, while a loss would drop the team to 29 percent, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . home.blurb: Macdonald clarified it is the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said. The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Bleacher Report • 17h Malachi Toney Out 4 Weeks Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, head coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday. Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week. Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1). home.blurb: Seahawks-Cardinals injury report: Leonard Williams held out with stinger, Drew Lock still limited - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Seahawks had six players miss practice with injury, including quarterback Sam Darnold , left tackle Charles Cross and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams. "Big Cat" was held out with a stinger he suffered on Monday night against the Chicago Bears and would be a massive loss for the team, especially in the run game. Nose tackle Brandon Pili also did not practice with a back injury, leaving Seattle thin at the position and facing a red-hot running back in Tyler Allgeier. With Darnold out, Seahawks Mike Macdonald indicated that backup Drew Lock would start in his place . Lock has been battling an elbow injury for the last three weeks, was inactive in their last two games, and was once again limited in practice on Wednesday with a right elbow injury. If Lock can't go, second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe would need to step in to make his first NFL start, which would be as entertaining as it would be stressful. Sticking with the offense, newly acquired star guard Quenton Nelson was limited by a knee injury, as was backup Anthony Bradford. With Josh Jones poised to start another week at left tackle, more offensive line injuries have to be the last thing Seahawks fans want to see. While wide receiver Rashid Shaheed was held out of practice and appears on track to miss his second straight game, his backup Tory Horton was a full go with a hand injury. Take the good news where you can get it! The report proves to be a mixed bag for the Seahawks defense as well. Edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who missed last week, was limited with an ankle injury, and Nick Emmanwori was a full participant with a shoulder injury. Those two returning to form in the lineup would be a massive boost for the "Dark Side" defense that is reeling from giving up 34 points on Monday. As for the Cardinals, breakout wide receiver Michael Wilson was limited in practice by rest and a rib injury, which could give him a chance to play on Sunday. Wilson broke two ribs and put up 111 yards and a touchdown on eight catches in Arizona's win over the Dallas Cowboys last week. Defensive tackle Walter Nolen was also limited with an ankle injury. Arizona will likely be without running back Bam Knight, who would back up Allgeier, as he did not practice on Wednesday due to a concussion. The Cardinals held stars Budda Baker and Josh Sweat out of practice, but it was not injury-related. Humorously, the Cardinals held quarterback Jacoby Brissett out with "rest," which apparently means getting shipped off to the Baltimore Ravens . Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Wemby makes NBA history First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.blurb: Vikings Predicted to ‘Soft’ Bench Starting QB Kyler Murray Against Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Wemby makes NBA history First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire Vikings Predicted to ‘Soft’ Bench Starting QB Kyler Murray Against Bills Quarterback Kyler Murray of the Minnesota Vikings. Getty Nathan Dougherty · HEAVY Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:14 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings could be making a change at quarterback for this week's game against the Buffalo Bills. The Vikings have struggled at times on offense despite a 6-1 start, leaning on a league-best defense to cover up the inefficiencies behind quarterback Kyler Murray. One NFL insider believes the Vikings could be planning to "soft" bench Murray for this weekend's game, using his lingering injury as an excuse to turn to veteran Carson Wentz. Vikings Could Make Change for Bills Game Vikings offensive coorindator Wes Phillips said after last week's loss to the Detroit Lions that his team has "got to get better" and would be looking at making some changes. "We're going to actively pursue every avenue we can to make that happen," Phillips said. While Phillips didn't point to any specific changes, NFL analyst Mike Florio suggested that the team could be using Murray's lingering hamstring tightness as an excuse to make a change at quarterback. "It's hard not to look at the current status of Murray's hamstring "tightness" as cover for a soft benching of Murray," Florio wrote . "That gives the Vikings a chance to let Carson Wentz, who played well enough in most of the Week 1 win over the Packers and all of the Week 2 win over the Bears." Florio added that Wentz has the best track record of success with top wide receiver Justin Jefferson . "We can't underestimate this Justin Jefferson wrinkle," Florio added. "Of all the quarterbacks they've had the past few years since Kirk Cousins, the one who has the best and most consistent connection with Justin Jefferson is Carson Wentz." Bills Made Changes on Defense The Vikings will face a Bills team that made some significant changes on defense. The team announced this week that they were releasing safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who struggled in coverage and was coming off a one-game suspension for spitting on a Las Vegas Raiders player. The Bills could instead turn to veteran safety Geno Stone , who was elevated from the practice squad for last week's win over the Baltimore Ravens . Stone played in 19 snaps on defense, making six tackles with one pass defensed, while also playing on special teams. Some insiders believe the Bills will seek more help before the NFL trade deadline, though any additions likely wouldn't be ready to contribute for Monday's game against the Vikings. The Bills could instead look to Tre'Davious White for help, with a potential practice squad elevation for the veteran cornerback who returned to the team in late October. away.blurb: When asked what it meant to him to be back out there, he was quick to respond. "Everything!" "Meant everything. I got the jitters when I first stepped on the field and then I got the jitters out even more when I fumbled and I was like, 'All right, now it's time to really lock back in and get going,'" the WR1 shared . "So, I was nervous at first and then went out there and just was like, 'All right, this is the game that I love and was good.'" Head coach Joe Brady spoke to the impact that Moore's return had as well as his importance to the Buffalo offense. He limped off the field after that play, and went to the medical tent to get checked out, before returning. Though he again showed a limp leaving the field after the game, he says he is okay. "You play a lot of games in this league. You're nervous because of coming back from the injury or just cuz you haven't been out there," he added. "It's more because of the injury and not being out there. So, l'm like, 'Dang, am I in game shape?' And today I found out I was." home.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR.
